claim: Board 170:17's note (170:28) states "Scoped runs touch only the selection. Clearing the selection widens it to the page." — an element-scoped run is drawn as a run that can only touch that element.
truth: False in the half that matters. Element scope constrains only the ELEMENT commands. Three of the fourteen commands the model is told about carry no elementId and are validated BEFORE the scope guard, so an element-scoped run can rewrite the page's meta title, meta description or URL slug, and can propose a live production publish. The second sentence IS true (deselect → {kind:"page"}).
evidence: server/services/ai.service.ts:1114-1122 extractValidEditCommands builds `allowedIds = new Set([elementId])`; isValidEditCommand returns EARLY for `set-page-setting` (branch at the top of the function, ai.service.ts:1268-1275: slug regex + SEO_LIMITS only) and for `propose-action` (ai.service.ts:1281-1284: `AGENT_PROPOSABLE_ACTIONS.has(actionId)` only) — neither touches allowedIds. buildEditCommandPrompt (ai.service.ts:906-909) joins EVERY `agentCallable` rule, and all 14 specs are `agentCallable: true` (ai.service.ts:823-900), so the element-scope prompt literally tells the model about set-page-setting and propose-action. Client side: applySetStyle.ts:647-650 pulls propose-action out of the batch and AITab.tsx:188 hands it to actionGate.propose, which opens a ConfirmDialog whose confirm deploys the site (useAiActionGate.ts:63-81). set-token is the one that IS safe under element scope: allowedTokens defaults to an empty Map (ai.service.ts:1256) so every tokenId fails membership. useAIScope.ts:32-35 confirms the deselect→page half.
edit: Rewrite TEXT node 170:28. Old: "Scoped runs touch only the selection. Clearing the selection widens it to the page." New: "Scoped runs edit only the selection — but page settings (title, description, slug) and a publish request are not element edits and can still come back. Clearing the selection widens the scope to the page." Keep the node's frame (170:27) at 280x44; the new string needs 280x60, so grow 170:27 to h=60 and push everything below by 16.

claim: Board 171:105 says "AI is out of credit for this month." (171:133) and "Nothing was changed. Your plan resets on 1 Aug, or upgrade to keep going." (171:134) — a monthly credit pool with a calendar reset date.
truth: The limit that blocks in-editor AI is DAILY, not monthly, and it resets at the next UTC midnight — never on a plan anniversary. FREE = 10 prompts/day, PRO = 200/day, BUSINESS = unlimited. The panel does not render the board's second sentence at all: it prints the server's own line verbatim, which is an ISO 8601 timestamp.
evidence: server/services/quota.service.ts:17-28 `todayBucket()` is a UTC day key and `nextMidnightUTC()` is the reset; reserveQuota reads `PLAN_LIMITS[plan].aiPromptsPerDay` (quota.service.ts:80). lib/constants/plan-limits.ts:35 FREE aiPromptsPerDay: 10, :56 PRO 200, :77 BUSINESS -1. server/trpc/routers/ai.ts:300-303 throws TOO_MANY_REQUESTS with `Daily limit reached (${quota.limit}). Resets at ${quota.resetsAt.toISOString()}.` AITab.tsx:284 renders the title as "AI is out of credit." (no "for this month") and AITab.tsx:288 renders `Nothing was changed. {stream.error}` — i.e. the ISO string, not "1 Aug".
edit: 171:133: "AI is out of credit for this month." -> "AI is out of credit." 171:134: "Nothing was changed. Your plan resets on 1 Aug, or upgrade to keep going." -> "Nothing was changed. Daily limit reached (10). Resets at midnight UTC." (sample values, shape is the contract). Apply the same correction to caption 172:42, which repeats the monthly framing.

claim: The run boards give a run four outcomes: it finishes (171:67), the user stops it (171:36), a step fails (171:2), or it pauses at a gate (170:97). Every one of them is an ending the user can see.
truth: There is a fifth: the run never ends. The agent path calls runPromptOnce, which registers onData and onError only — no onConnectionStateChange — so it never sees the retryable-reconnect path that useStreamPrompt was explicitly fixed to catch. A provider outage during planning or during any step leaves phase pinned on "planning"/"running" with the band reading "Planning" or "Running · N of M" forever, no error card, and no timeout. The only exit is Stop.
evidence: runPromptOnce.ts:83-109 — the subscribe callbacks are exactly `onData` and `onError`. useStreamPrompt.ts:69-83 documents why that is not enough: "tRPC's SSE client treats INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR as RETRYABLE (`retryableRpcCodes` in @trpc/server) and silently reconnects instead of calling `onError` … Measured against a real dev server: one EventSource, five opens, five errors, zero data, sixteen seconds, no error on screen." and adds the handler at :150-159 with a 2-attempt budget. useAgentRunner.ts:250 (plan) and :166 (each step) both await runPromptOnce, so neither can ever reject on that path.

Band reads "RUNNING · 2 OF 3" unchanged; add a 280x60 note frame under the Stop row reading "The provider stopped answering. Nothing has failed and nothing will finish — Stop is the only way out." Wire 170:41 and 170:70 to it as a second outcome alongside the existing hotspots, and wire it to 171:36 (stopped) via Stop.

claim: Board 170:2's note (170:16) reads "AI proposes a diff and never writes directly. Each Apply lands as one undo step — a multi-step draft applies one step at a time." It is the family's governing promise and it is stated without qualification.
truth: Sentence two is true and verified. Sentence one is not true of the product as a whole: an AI writes to the user's project with no diff, no Apply and no board, on every image upload. useAltTextAutoTrigger fires media.generateAltText the moment an image finishes uploading and writes the result straight into the asset via composer.media.updateAsset. No surface announces it, nothing gates it, and there is no way to turn it off.
evidence: useAltTextAutoTrigger.ts:44-80 — subscribes to MEDIA_EVENTS.UPLOAD_COMPLETE at mount, calls generateAltTextRemote(asset.serverId) and then `await composer.media.updateAsset(asset.id, { altText: result.altText, generatedMetadata: … })`. Mounted at StudioPanels (per its own docstring, :18-19) so it covers uploads from the Media tab, canvas drag-drop and paste. Not behind any feature flag — grep for isFeatureEnabled in that file returns nothing. The undo half IS true: applySetStyle.ts:642-661 opens one transaction per applyAiEdit call, and useAgentRunner.ts:280 calls applyAiEdit once per approved step, so a 3-step run is 3 undo entries — which is exactly what 170:16's tail already says.
edit: 170:16: keep sentences 2 and 3 verbatim. Replace sentence 1: "AI proposes a diff and never writes directly." -> "AI proposes a diff for anything you ask it to change. (Alt text for a new image is written automatically — that one is not a proposal.)" Frame 170:15 grows 280x60 -> 280x76.

claim: The gate panel (170:121) says "Step 3 replaces an image you uploaded." (170:122) and "This one cannot be undone by re-running. Approve it, or skip it and keep the rest." (170:123) — a per-step consequence assessment.
truth: The product computes no consequence and has no risk model. The gate renders the step's own plan title and instruction: "Step {n}: {plan.title}" and "{plan.instruction} Approve it, or skip it and keep the rest." The board's first clause is a sentence nothing can produce, and "cannot be undone by re-running" is contradicted by the family's own Undo-all control.
evidence: AgentPlan.tsx:191-196 — `Step {currentIndex + 1}: {gateStep.plan.title}` then `{gateStep.plan.instruction} Approve it, or skip it and keep the rest.` PlanStep is `{title, scope, instruction}` (runPromptOnce.ts:13-17) — no risk, severity or undoability field anywhere. The only undoability metadata in the whole AI surface is ai-actions.service.ts:60 `undoable: false` on site.publish, which is a privileged ACTION, not a plan step, and never reaches this panel.

Approve it, or skip it and keep the rest." -> "Replace the hero image with the warm interior shot. Approve it, or skip it and keep the rest." (the instruction is sample; the SHAPE — plan instruction + fixed tail — is the contract).

claim: The two error boards, 171:105 and 171:136, are the family's account of quota exhaustion and a missing key.
truth: Neither can be reached from an agent run. On the agent path the failure travels through runPromptOnce, which flattens every tRPC error to `new Error(err.message)` and drops the error CODE, so useAgentRunner cannot tell a quota block from a missing key from a bad step. All three land in AgentPlan's amber "step failed" card with Undo-all and Retry — and a quota block that hits during PLANNING produces a card with no step number at all, since failedIndex is -1.
evidence: runPromptOnce.ts:102-107 — `onError: (err: { message?: string }) => … reject(new Error(err.message ?? "Stream failed"))`; the parameter type does not even include `data.code`, which is what useStreamPrompt.ts:134-142 switches on to produce errorKind. useAgentRunner.ts:223 `setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "That step failed.")` and :268 `setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Planning failed")`. AgentPlan.tsx:213-241 renders one card for every value of `error`; :216 prints `Step {failedIndex+1} failed — {error}` when a step is marked failed and the bare `{error}` otherwise, and :218 suppresses the "Nothing after step N ran" line when failedIndex < 0. The server's quota string is the one that arrives (ai.ts:300-303).
edit: Add a plan-failure variant of 170:41: "AI · planning-failed", 280x812, cloned from 170:41 with the step rows and Actions removed and an amber card carrying "Daily limit reached (10). Resets at 2026-09-07T00:00:00.000Z." plus a Retry — the raw shape the code produces. Caption it as a defect to be closed in code (the agent path should route errorKind the way useStreamPrompt does), not a design to keep.

claim: Coverage record: the shipped agent loop, state by state, against the boards.
truth: A run is: start(prompt) -> phase "planning" (one plan call) -> phase "running", and per step generate -> either an edit (auto-apply on: apply and advance; auto-apply off: status "awaiting", the gate) or no edit (status "nochange", advance) -> approve (applyAiEdit, one transaction, status "applied") or skip (status "skipped") -> advance; last step, user Stop, or a step failure ends it at phase "done". Seven step statuses (pending, running, awaiting, applied, skipped, nochange, failed), four phases (idle, planning, running, done) plus the stoppedByUser flag that tells a stopped run from a finished one. Boards drawn: planning 170:41, running 170:70, step-gate 170:97, step-failed 171:2, stopped 171:36, done 171:67. Not drawn, in this row's scope: agent-idle (W-K-25), auto-apply on (W-K-15), nochange (W-K-20), run-stalled (FIG-K-04), the gate's diff (FIG-K-07). Undo is per-step by construction and both the board and the code say so.
evidence: useAgentRunner.ts:32-47 (StepStatus, RunPhase), :236-273 start, :144-233 generateStep, :275-287 approve, :289-294 skip, :296-302 stop, :304-312 reset, :134-142 advance.
